0.0.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

1.0.n: Combines with たち to refer to the speaker and her group.

1.1.n: Added to 私 to make 私たち, meaning we.

1.2.n: 首 means neck, but here it begins the group name 首ンセス.

1.3.n: This is the rest of the group name 首ンセス, not a separate word.

1.4.n: A polite ending identifying the speakers as 首ンセス.

2.0.n: Sets the time for the group's outing.

2.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic: what follows concerns today.

2.2.n: Describes this outing as a first experience for the group.

2.3.n: 首 begins the group name 首ンセス; it is not a separate reference to a neck here.

2.4.n: Completes the group name 首ンセス.

2.5.n: Links the group name to メンバー, identifying which group's members they are.

2.6.n: An English loanword; Japanese does not require a plural ending here.

2.7.n: Marks the group participating in the outing together.

2.8.n: A noun from 出かける, with お adding a friendly, polite tone.

2.9.n: Connects the outing description to こと as part of ということで.

2.10.n: Packages the preceding description as a situation in ということで.

2.11.n: Completes ということで, presenting the outing as the background for their plans.

3.0.n: 首 begins the group name, setting up the connection with necks later in the sentence.

3.1.n: Completes the group name 首ンセス.

3.2.n: Marks 首ンセス as what their choice is connected to.

3.3.n: The て-form of ちなむ connects their clothing choice to the group's name.

3.4.n: Here 首 is an ordinary noun, echoing the neck character in their group name.

3.5.n: Marks 首 as what looks beautiful.

3.6.n: Written in katakana here; describes the appearance of their necks.

3.7.n: Makes キレイ describe how their necks look with 見える.

3.8.n: Describes how something appears; 首がキレイに見える modifies 着物.

3.9.n: The preceding description specifies kimonos in which their necks look beautiful.

3.10.n: Marks 着物 as what they wear.

3.11.n: The connecting stem of 着る joins ながら to describe wearing something during another activity.

3.12.n: Attaches to 着 to show that wearing kimonos happens during their exploring.

4.0.n: A place name for a district in Tokyo.

4.1.n: Marks 浅草 as the place they will explore.

4.2.n: 探索する becomes 探索して, adds いく for proceeding onward, and たい to express desire.

4.3.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

4.4.n: The polite form of 思う; after たいと, it softens the statement of what they want to do.

5.0.n: Originally the past form of やる, but used here as an excited cheer.

5.1.n: This mark stretches the final vowel of やった to express excitement.

5.3.n: Used alone as a casual exclamation, with です left out.

0.tip: こんにちは is a standard greeting, and its final は sounds like わ.

1.tip: 首ンセス is one group name, despite being split into two tappable pieces.

2.lit: Today, given that it is our first outing together as Kubinsesu members,
2.tip: ということで presents the situation as background for what they will do next.

3.lit: In keeping with Kubinsesu, while wearing kimonos in which our necks look beautiful,
3.tip: 着ながら means wearing while doing something else; the main activity comes in the next line.

4.lit: We think we want to go on exploring Asakusa!
4.tip: たいと思います is a polite, softened way to announce what you would like to do.

5.tip: 楽しみ can stand alone to express excitement about something coming up.
